name: robot_arm_mount_autonomous
description: Fully autonomous structural workflow — the prompt describes geometry + service context only. The agent must derive ALL boundary conditions itself (fixed supports, loads, moments, bearing seat) and declare them in spec.load_cases, plus declare the machined interfaces in spec.features. fem/optimize/refine stages declare NOTHING (use_parent_fallbacks): fem_loadcases verifies the resolved physics of the agent's own load model, topopt optimizes on it, refine re-cuts the agent-declared features via spec_features fallback.

stages.prompt:
Mounting bracket for a robot-arm joint (aluminium 6061), parametric — input for topology optimization.

Frame: base plate on the XY plane (z = 0), centred in X and Y. mm.
- Base plate 100 x 80 x 10.
- 4 holes dia 8.5 along Z at (x=+/-42, y=+/-32) — mounting bolts.
- Bearing boss dia 25 x 15 tall on the plate centre (top at z = 25) with an M12 tapped (internal thread, M12x1.75) through-bore along Z — model the bore at tap-drill size and declare the thread; the export rebuild carries the real thread groove — threaded shaft seat.
- Vertical flange at the +X edge on the plate: 8 thick, 40 wide (y-centred), 30 tall (z = 10..40); two dia 6.5 holes along X at (y=+/-12, z=25).
- One gusset rib 5 mm thick at y = 0 joining boss and flange.
Symmetric in Y.

SERVICE CONTEXT — derive the structural model yourself: the bracket is bolted to a rigid frame through the four base holes; the boss bore is the shaft seat that carries the arm — typical service is a downward arm weight of several hundred N on the seat plus an occasional overturning moment on the order of 100 Nm; the two flange pin holes carry link forces of a few hundred N each. YOU decide the load cases, the fixed supports, the load regions/mechanisms and the magnitudes — declare them all in spec.load_cases (fixed regions on the bolt interfaces, loads on the seat/bore/flange features). Also declare every machined interface (bolt holes, tapped bore, flange pin holes) in spec.features with position, axis, diameter and depth so the post-optimization refinement can re-cut them exactly.
